properties.description: The function-preservation check refuses what it cannot classify (crates/reflow2-core/tests/preserve.rs) — 15 cases. The suite defends the REFUSAL half, because a classifier that recognises ALLOCATED_TO and calls everything else benign hands out green certificates for changes it never looked at (BL-170's fourth quadrant). So: an unknown node type blocks certification, an unresolvable edge endpoint blocks it, a reworded capability blocks it (a rename and a scope change are the same bytes), and a known function change OUTRANKS an unknown, because more information cannot un-move a capability. `every_schema_node_type_has_a_class` walks the live schema — all 29 types — and fails the build when a new one lands with no class, so the omission is caught before a release rather than by a false green; it also asserts three known types are present, so it cannot pass by iterating an empty set. The load-bearing case is `depends_on_is_read_from_its_endpoints_not_its_type`: DEPENDS_ON is the functional DAG between Capabilities and packaging between Components, and classifying by edge type alone would file all 51 of this design's cross-system dependencies as function changes.
properties.findings: MUTATION-CHECKED against four seeded regressions (unknown types falling back to structure, the verdict order inverted, one function endpoint sufficing for a function edge, a reworded function node waved through) — each was caught, none silently.
properties.name: The function-preservation check refuses what it cannot classify
